newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ukraine's Kuchma seeks strategic ties with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma seeks strategic ties with Russia.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma called in an interview screened on Saturday for Kiev and Moscow to put aside their dispute over the Black Sea fleet and sign an agreement on strategic partnership in the region.

Ukraine and Russia have been unable to resolve a long-running row over division of the former Soviet fleet and the dispute has been the main obstacle to a keynote political agreement being signed between the two Slav neighbours.

"In my view all politicians should stop their talks and sign an agreement on friendship and cooperation, where the strategic partnership of Ukraine and Russia is written in black and white -- that would envisage strategic partnership in the Black Sea region," Kuchma told Russian Public Television.
Kiev and Moscow have been arguing since the Soviet union collapsed in 1991 over how to split the 600 ships.

Kuchma and President Boris Yeltsin seemed to have achieved a breakthrough in October, even though the Russian State Duma lower house of parliament voted to cancel the division in a vote that was not legally binding.
Asked if he wanted the fleet question taken out of the framework of the wider treaty, Kuchma said; "Absolutely so."

"It is still not possible to find a solution which would satisfy both sides on the division of the fleet ... but all the same it is possible to find a solution which will talk about strategic partnership," he said.

Most of the argument has concerned the control of the fleet's bases in and around the city of Sevastopol on the Crimean peninsula rather than the ships. Broad agreements have already been signed on dividing the fleet.
Kuchma said the division of the fleet was already a fact but that it left neither the Russian nor Ukrainian fleets in a state to carry out their tasks in the region.
